analysis:
Compared the supplied BASE/HEAD Serve.swift source and ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift patch, BASE source and metadata. Serve.swift:429-430 now records receipt of coordinator inference requests in the fast connection-control reader, before FIFO admission. The recovery patch adds a connected-only lastRequestAt update (HEAD:17-19) and replaces the previous authorization predicate with ServingReadiness.verdict (HEAD:31-48): only blocked connections with advertised models enter reconnect supervision; authorized verdicts reset attempts, while pending/unconfirmed verdicts clear the refusal timer. Existing reconnect idle/update checks remain unchanged in BASE:39-55.
No concrete regression is established here. Request observation does not visibly grant serving permission, decrypt data, bypass admission or change terminal accounting. Connection events still immediately clear authorization (Serve.swift:425-428), while inference, cancellation and disconnect cleanup retain FIFO ordering. Registration key binding, fresh attestation creation, privacy claims, cache-scope forwarding, SSD maintenance and shutdown paths are unchanged in the supplied comparison. Relevant contracts are TB-002/TB-011, T-052/T-053/T-057 and A-018; no changed cache exposure under T-041 is visible.
Integration must examine ServingReadiness.verdict and DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt initialization/persistence alongside authorization admission checks. In particular, verify that receipt before admission is only routing evidence, cannot extend expired/revoked permission, is reset across sessions, and that pending/unconfirmed verdicts do not suppress required recovery indefinitely. These implementations are outside this supplied scope, so the availability and authorization consequences of the new verdict-driven supervision remain unresolved, not proven vulnerabilities.
